items.title: Harold E. Peterson Interview, 1979-08-06
items.q: He said, man, your friend got killed. He's killed, I said

ctx.x: This fella used to, when he'd go on a job, this is the truth, he used to have a second line following him. Kids, see, second line. So, he used to come around the store all the time, and him and I would get on the drums, you know what I mean. And, one night he played a job, and after the job where he was living, he went down to the corner to get a bottle of pop. Wasn't no drinking fella, pop now, root beer or something. And while he's in there, some fella comes in there and kills him. And he's on the ground, and…

That fella was the American, one of the finest drummers I have ever heard, white or black, I'm telling you the truth. The guy was great. Man, man, I said, look at this boy, ain't that a shame? But that's what they were telling me. Now, he never came around the store anymore after that, so it had to be true.
